title: Being called a parlor musician who read music
summary: He explains he learned by reading, not by ear, and other bands like Sam Morgan's and Chris Kelly's came to him for music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Oh I see, what did that mean?

You see I wasn't a head man so much. I see. You understand? I see the music, now if I see the music I play with it about two or three times, well I'd get the chorus. Then I'd have it. Then I'd have it. With the voice I couldn't get it, you understand? As long as I get it, play it two or three times and get that chorus then I'd start on it. But you had to see the music, you see. But some fellows would hear the singing again, but I'd rather play by the music.

A parlor. They called me a parlor. They used to call me a parlor music. But after a while all of them would come by the parlor music. Yeah. Yeah, a musician. They used to call me a parlor musician because I used to play all the music, you understand? And like the piano and the thing, you put the coffee up there and play it. You see, that one used to call me a parlor musician. Yeah. But when they come to parlor, when they had to read, they all of them come to me. Every one of them, every one of them come to me. For the light of this, the light of that. Sam Morgan, all of them little bands, Rene, Chris Kelly, all of them little bands, all of them little bands, all of them little bands come to me. But still they used to call me a parlor, a parlor musician. But when they find out, they was getting them tuned so fast, you understand? They couldn't think of them. Then they come to me and want a light. Yeah. Yeah. Some of them would know the music. Some of them know the music just as good, but they didn't know the division. Yeah, they didn't know the division. See, the division is the principal part.
It's by the… Yeah. The music. The count of the lives.
